assignedReviews.card_evidence: A follicle is a sac-like structure inside a woman's ovary where one egg cell starts to mature.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe a valence electron as an electron in the outer shell of an atom that can take part in formation of bonds
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the biological structure of an ovarian follicle and egg maturation. G9-M-3 is about valence electrons in the outer shell of an atom and chemical bonding, which is entirely unrelated to the card's content.

copy.en: A follicle is a sac-like structure inside a woman's ovary where one egg cell starts to mature.
copy.tl: Ang follicle ay parang sac na structure sa loob ng ovary ng babae kung saan nagsisimulang mag-mature ang isang egg cell.
copy.bis: Ang follicle usa ka sama sa sac nga structure sa sulod sa ovary sa babaye diin magsugod pag-mature ang usa ka egg cell.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A food allergen warning on a label tells consumers about ingredients, like peanuts, that may cause an allergy.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about food allergen labeling, not about chemical properties of materials such as being burnt, reacting, or being degradable/biodegradable. No instructional support for G4-M-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A food allergen warning on a label tells consumers about ingredients, like peanuts, that may cause an allergy.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate ways to minimize harmful changes in materials, such as restriction of burning of waste materials, and care in handling reactive materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses informing consumers about allergens, not demonstrating ways to minimize harmful changes in materials (e.g., restricting burning, handling reactive materials). No instructional support for G4-M-5.

copy.en: A food allergen warning on a label tells consumers about ingredients, like peanuts, that may cause an allergy.
copy.tl: Ang food allergen warning sa isang label ay nagsasabi sa mga mamimili tungkol sa mga sangkap, tulad ng mani, na maaaring magdulot ng allergy.
copy.bis: Ang food allergen warning sa usa ka label nagsulti sa mga konsumidor mahitungod sa mga sangkap, sama sa mani, nga mahimong makapahinabog allergy.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Eat high-fiber foods like fruits, vegetables, and whole grains
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses foods for a healthy digestive system, which is unrelated to electricity as a flow of electrons or safe handling of electricity. The assigned competency is in the Force, Motion, and Energy domain and has no connection to digestive health.

copy.en:
What foods should I eat to keep my digestive system healthy?

Eat high-fiber foods like fruits, vegetables, and whole grains, and drink plenty of water to help waste move through your system easily.
copy.tl:
Anong mga pagkain ang dapat kong kainin para mapanatiling malusog ang digestive system ko?

Kumain ng mga pagkaing mataas sa fiber tulad ng prutas, gulay, at whole grains, at uminom ng maraming tubig para madaling makalabas ang dumi sa sistema mo.
copy.bis:
Unsa nga mga pagkaon ang angay nakong kan-on aron magpabiling himsog ang akong digestive system?

Pagkaon sa mga pagkaon nga taas ug fiber sama sa prutas, utanon, ug whole grains, ug pag-inom ug daghang tubig aron sayon nga mogawas ang hugaw sa imong sistema.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: using it to measure distance gives different results because feet come in many sizes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about measuring distance with a foot span, not about making objects move by natural causes or by people. It does not support the competency's skill of exploring/demonstrating ways to move objects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A foot span is the length of a person's foot
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses measurement using a body part, not matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. No connection to the concept of matter.

copy.en: A foot span is the length of a person's foot, and using it to measure distance gives different results because feet come in many sizes.
copy.tl: Ang foot span ay ang haba ng paa ng isang tao, at ang paggamit nito sa pagsukat ng distansya ay nagbibigay ng magkakaibang resulta dahil iba-iba ang laki ng mga paa.
copy.bis: Ang foot span mao ang gitas-on sa tiil sa usa ka tawo, ug ang paggamit niini sa pagsukod sa distansya maghatag ug managlahi nga resulta tungod kay lainlain ang gidak-on sa mga tiil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Force can cause a physical change, like crumpling paper into a ball, which changes its shape but not its composition.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the advantage of high biodiversity in maintaining the stability of an ecosystem during difficult conditions, such as food shortages, disease, and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about force causing a physical change in an object (paper). It has no content about biodiversity, ecosystem stability, or difficult conditions such as food shortages, disease, or climate change. The assigned competency is entirely unrelated to the card's subject.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Force can cause a physical change, like crumpling paper into a ball, which changes its shape but not its composition.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a physical change caused by force on a non-living object. It does not address interactions between living things or between living and non-living things, nor any good or harm to living things. The competency is unrelated to the card's content.

copy.en: Force can cause a physical change, like crumpling paper into a ball, which changes its shape but not its composition.
copy.tl: Ang puwersa ay maaaring magdulot ng physical change, tulad ng paglamukot ng papel na nagiging bola, na nagbabago ang hugis ngunit hindi ang komposisyon.
copy.bis: Ang puwersa mahimong hinungdan sa physical change, sama sa paglumok sa papel nga mahimong bola, nga mausab ang porma apan dili ang komposisyon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: you add more force and the ball moves faster
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate sexual from asexual reproduction in terms of: a) number of parents involved, and b) similarities of offspring to parents
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how applying force changes the speed of a moving ball, a physics/motion concept. G7-L-7 requires differentiating sexual from asexual reproduction by number of parents and offspring similarity, which is entirely unrelated to the card content.

copy.en: If you keep pushing a ball while it is already rolling, you add more force and the ball moves faster.
copy.tl: Kung patuloy mong itinutulak ang bola habang ito ay gumugulong na, nagdadagdag ka ng force kaya mas bibilis ang bola.
copy.bis: Kung padayon nimo nga itulod ang bola samtang kini nagligid na, magdugang ka og force busa mas mopaspas ang bola.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You use force in daily activities like walking, lifting objects, throwing a ball, or moving things to a particular direction.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about everyday uses of force, with no mention of the Sun, Moon, planets, stars, or any celestial objects observed in the sky.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You use force in daily activities like walking, lifting objects, throwing a ball, or moving things to a particular direction.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from local indigenous community members or from reliable secondary sources to investigate ways that indigenous people of the Philippines represented and communicated understandings of the predictability of solar and lunar eclipses, and patterns/interpretations in the night sky and their use for tracking time
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses force in daily activities and has no content about indigenous knowledge, eclipses, night sky patterns, or time tracking.

copy.en: You use force in daily activities like walking, lifting objects, throwing a ball, or moving things to a particular direction.
copy.tl: Gumagamit ka ng force sa pang-araw-araw na gawain tulad ng paglalakad, pagbubuhat ng mga bagay, paghagis ng bola, o paglipat ng mga bagay sa isang direksyon.
copy.bis: Gigamit nimo ang force sa adlaw-adlaw nga mga buluhaton sama sa paglakaw, pag-alsa sa mga butang, paglabay sa bola, o pagbalhin sa mga butang ngadto sa usa ka direksyon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Objects with greater momentum require a greater force to stop
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains momentum and stopping force, which is physics content. G8-L-9 requires describing photosynthesis and respiration and identifying raw materials and products. There is no connection to living things or these processes.

copy.en: Objects with greater momentum require a greater force to stop, assuming the stopping time is the same.
copy.tl: Ang mga bagay na may mas malaking momentum ay nangangailangan ng mas malakas na puwersa para tumigil, kung pareho ang oras ng pagtigil.
copy.bis: Ang mga butang nga adunay mas dako nga momentum nagkinahanglan ug mas kusog nga puwersa aron mohunong, kung pareho ang oras sa paghunong.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Intermolecular forces, the pulls between particles, are extremely weak in gases
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses intermolecular forces in gases, a physics/chemistry topic. G3-L-4 requires observing and describing animal outer body parts (head, legs, wings) and their roles in movement and food gathering. There is no connection to animal anatomy or living things.

copy.en: Intermolecular forces, the pulls between particles, are extremely weak in gases, so gas particles move about freely.
copy.tl: Ang intermolecular forces, ang hatakan sa pagitan ng mga particle, ay napakahina sa gas, kaya malayang gumagalaw ang mga particle ng gas.
copy.bis: Ang intermolecular forces, ang pagbira tali sa mga particle, hilabihan kahuyang sa gas, mao nga gawasnon nga molihok ang mga particle sa gas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Particles of matter attract each other, and this force of attraction is strongest in solids and weakest in gases.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure and describe changes in the position of people or objects in relation to their original position, such as moving closer, farther, left, or right
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the force of attraction between particles of matter, a concept from the particle model of matter (G7-M-3). It does not address measuring or describing changes in position of people or objects relative to an original position, which is the focus of G3-F-3.

copy.en: Particles of matter attract each other, and this force of attraction is strongest in solids and weakest in gases.
copy.tl: Ang mga particles ng matter ay umaakit sa isa't isa, at ang puwersa ng atraksyon na ito ay pinakamalakas sa solids at pinakamahina sa gases.
copy.bis: Ang mga particles sa matter nag-attract sa usag usa, ug kini nga puwersa sa atraksyon labing kusog sa solids ug labing huyang sa gases.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most Ford Model T cars were painted black because it kept them cheap and helped speed up production!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the color of a car model, not about a famous scientist or their invention. It does not support identifying a scientist or an invention.

copy.en: Most Ford Model T cars were painted black because it kept them cheap and helped speed up production!
copy.tl: Karamihan sa Ford Model T ay kulay itim para makamura at mapabilis ang paggawa ng mga kotse!
copy.bis: Kadaghanan sa Ford Model T itom ang kolor aron magbarato ug mapaspas ang paghimo sa mga awto!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: How do you write a formula from a name like dinitrogen trioxide?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the indicators for a chemical reaction as color change, the formation of a precipitate, the release of gas, and or odor, or a change in temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches how to write a chemical formula from a name using prefixes. It does not address indicators of a chemical reaction (color change, precipitate, gas, odor, temperature change).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: How do you write a formula from a name like dinitrogen trioxide?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the formation of new bonds or the breaking of existing bonds constitutes a chemical change and the formation of a new substance
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about converting a compound name to a formula, not about bond formation/breaking constituting a chemical change or formation of a new substance.

copy.en:
How do you write a formula from a name like dinitrogen trioxide?

The prefix di- means 2 nitrogen atoms, and tri- means 3 oxygen atoms, so the formula is N2O3!
copy.tl:
Paano isinusulat ang formula mula sa pangalang dinitrogen trioxide?

Ang prefix na di- ay nangangahulugang 2 nitrogen atoms, at ang tri- ay nangangahulugang 3 oxygen atoms, kaya ang formula ay N2O3!
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagsulat ang formula gikan sa ngalang dinitrogen trioxide?

Ang prefix nga di- nagpasabot og 2 ka nitrogen atoms, ug ang tri- nagpasabot og 3 ka oxygen atoms, busa ang formula kay N2O3!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: What is the difference between formula mass and molecular mass?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses formula mass vs molecular mass, a chemistry concept. G4-M-1 requires identifying a famous scientist and their invention, which is entirely unrelated.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: What is the difference between formula mass and molecular mass?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify inertia as the tendency for an object to stay at rest or in motion unless acted on by an unbalanced net force
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about mass concepts in chemistry, not about inertia or Newton's laws. G9-F-1 concerns inertia as the tendency to stay at rest or in motion, which is not addressed.

copy.en: What is the difference between formula mass and molecular mass?\n\nFormula mass is used for ionic compounds and expressed in amu, while molecular mass is used for covalent compounds and expressed in g/mol.
copy.tl: Ano ang pagkakaiba ng formula mass at molecular mass?\n\nAng formula mass ay ginagamit para sa ionic compounds at sinusukat sa amu, habang ang molecular mass ay para sa covalent compounds at sinusukat sa g/mol.
copy.bis: Unsa ang kalainan sa formula mass ug molecular mass?\n\nAng formula mass gigamit para sa ionic compounds ug gisukod sa amu, samtang ang molecular mass para sa covalent compounds ug gisukod sa g/mol.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Metallic crystals, ionic crystals, covalent crystals, and molecular crystals are four types of crystals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that momentum is conserved before and after the collision of objects
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes types of crystals and their bonds, which is a chemistry topic. G10-F-8 is about conservation of momentum in collisions, a physics topic. No overlap in content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Metallic crystals, ionic crystals, covalent crystals, and molecular crystals are four types of crystals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe different types of collisions as elastic or inelastic by providing some examples
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about crystal types, not about elastic or inelastic collisions. G10-F-2 requires describing collision types with examples, which the card does not address at all.

copy.en: Metallic crystals, ionic crystals, covalent crystals, and molecular crystals are four types of crystals with different particles and bonds.
copy.tl: Ang metallic crystals, ionic crystals, covalent crystals, at molecular crystals ay apat na uri ng crystals na may magkakaibang particles at bonds.
copy.bis: Ang metallic crystals, ionic crystals, covalent crystals, ug molecular crystals upat ka klase sa crystals nga adunay lain-laing particles ug bonds.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The fovea -- a tiny spot in the retina packed with cones
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about observing and describing the outer body parts of animals (head, legs, wings) and their role in movement and food gathering. The card describes the fovea, an internal part of the human eye, and its role in sharp vision. This is unrelated to outer body parts or movement/food gathering.

copy.en:
Which part of your eye sees the sharpest?

The fovea -- a tiny spot in the retina packed with cones -- that's why we look straight at things we want to see clearly.
copy.tl:
Aling bahagi ng mata ang pinakamatalas?

Ang fovea -- isang maliit na lugar sa retina na siksik sa cones -- kaya tinitingnan natin nang diretso ang gusto nating makitang malinaw.
copy.bis:
Unsang bahin sa mata ang pinaka-hait?

Ang fovea -- usa ka gamay nga dapit sa retina nga puno sa cones -- mao nga motan-aw ta og diretso sa gusto natong makita nga klaro.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why are fresh, home-prepared foods often better than processed foods?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a simple electromagnet and observe and record its properties
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the benefits of fresh foods over processed foods (preservatives/additives). It has no relation to making an electromagnet or observing its properties, which is the competency's subject.

copy.en:
Why are fresh, home-prepared foods often better than processed foods?

They usually have no added preservatives or additives, so you eat fewer extra chemicals!
copy.tl:
Bakit mas mainam ang sariwa at lutong bahay na pagkain kaysa processed food?

Karaniwang wala silang dagdag na preservatives o additives, kaya mas kaunting karagdagang kemikal ang nakakain mo!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga mas maayo ang presko ug giluto sa balay nga pagkaon kaysa processed food?

Kasagaran wala silay dugang nga preservatives o additives, busa mas diyutay nga dugang nga kemikal ang imong makaon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fruits differ in size, shape, color, and number
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify practical applications of electromagnetic radiation, such as radio waves used in telecommunications, and x-rays and gamma rays in medicine
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes variation in fruits (size, shape, color, number). G9-F-12 requires identifying practical applications of electromagnetic radiation (radio waves, x-rays, gamma rays). There is no connection to electromagnetic radiation or its applications; the content is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Fruits differ in size, shape, color, and number, from a tiny red berry to a big green watermelon with many seeds.
copy.tl: Ang mga bunga ay nagkakaiba sa laki, hugis, kulay, at bilang, mula sa maliit na pulang berry hanggang sa malaking berdeng pakwan na maraming buto.
copy.bis: Ang mga bunga managlahi sa gidak-on, porma, kolor, ug gidaghanon, gikan sa gamay nga pula nga berry hangtod sa dako nga berde nga pakwan nga daghan og liso.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Filipino scientist Julian Banzon discovered how to get oil from coconuts
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make drawings or a simple model to show the motion of the Earth and Moon relative to the Sun to explain the phases of the moon that people see from Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about a Filipino scientist's coconut oil discovery, which has no connection to the motion of the Earth and Moon relative to the Sun or the phases of the moon. The assigned competency is entirely unrelated to the card content.

copy.en:
Can we get fuel from a coconut?

Yes! Filipino scientist Julian Banzon discovered how to get oil from coconuts, which can be used as a source of fuel.
copy.tl:
Maaari ba tayong kumuha ng fuel mula sa niyog?

Oo! Natuklasan ng Pilipinong scientist na si Julian Banzon kung paano kumuha ng langis mula sa niyog, na maaaring gamitin bilang pinagmumulan ng fuel.
copy.bis:
Makakuha ba kita ug fuel gikan sa lubi?

Oo! Nadiskobrehan sa Pilipinong scientist nga si Julian Banzon kung unsaon pagkuha ug lana gikan sa lubi, nga mahimong gamiton isip tinubdan sa fuel.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some fungi are used as medicine, like penicillin, which is an antibiotic that kills bacteria causing infections.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses fungi as a source of medicine (penicillin) and its antibiotic effect on bacteria. It does not address chemical properties of materials such as burning, reacting with other materials, or being degradable/biodegradable. The content is biological/medical, not about material chemical properties.

copy.en: Some fungi are used as medicine, like penicillin, which is an antibiotic that kills bacteria causing infections.
copy.tl: Ang ilang fungi ay ginagamit bilang gamot, tulad ng penicillin, na isang antibiotic na pumapatay ng bacteria na nagdudulot ng impeksyon.
copy.bis: Ang uban nga fungi gigamit isip tambal, sama sa penicillin, nga usa ka antibiotic nga mopatay sa bacteria nga makapahinabo ug impeksyon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fur or feathers protect animals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate proper handling and disposal of materials according to their properties, such as reusing objects, disposing of excess oil into garbage, and recycling paper, plastic or glass
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes animal body coverings (fur/feathers) for temperature regulation. G3-M-7 is about proper handling and disposal of materials according to their properties (reusing, recycling, etc.). There is no instructional support for material handling or disposal.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fur or feathers protect animals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate ways to minimize harmful changes in materials, such as restriction of burning of waste materials, and care in handling reactive materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about animal adaptations, not about minimizing harmful changes in materials or handling reactive materials. G4-M-5 concerns restriction of burning waste and care with reactive materials, which is unrelated to fur/feathers.

copy.en: Fur or feathers protect animals from the heat of the sun and from cold nights, keeping their bodies comfortable.
copy.tl: Ang balahibo o mga pakpak na balahibo ay nagpoprotekta sa mga hayop mula sa init ng araw at sa malamig na gabi, para maging komportable ang kanilang katawan.
copy.bis: Ang balhibo o mga balhibo sa pako nagpanalipod sa mga mananap sa kainit sa adlaw ug sa kabugnaw sa gabii, aron magpabiling komportable ang ilang lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: wearing a mask keeps you from breathing in floating plant pollen
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about allergy safety and pollen avoidance; it does not identify or describe the parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or how they work, which is the exact competency.

copy.en: On dry, windy days, wearing a mask keeps you from breathing in floating plant pollen — the kind that can trigger allergic asthma.
copy.tl: Sa tuyo at maangin na araw, ang pagsusuot ng maskara ay pumipigil sa paglanghap ng lumilipad na pollen ng halaman — na maaaring magdulot ng allergic asthma.
copy.bis: Sa uga ug hangin nga adlaw, ang pagsul-ob og maskara mopugong sa pagsuyop og naglupad nga pollen sa tanom — nga makapahinabo og allergic asthma.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Remove a bee stinger by scraping it sideways with a card
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches first-aid removal of a bee stinger, not observation or description of animal outer body parts (head, legs, wings) or their roles in movement and food gathering. No direct or prerequisite support for the competency.

copy.en: Remove a bee stinger by scraping it sideways with a card — this stops the venom sac from pumping more poison into your skin.
copy.tl: Alisin ang tibo ng bubuyog sa pamamagitan ng pag-gasgas nito paskil gamit ang card — para hindi na makapag-pump pa ng lason ang venom sac sa balat mo.
copy.bis: Kuhaa ang tibo sa buyog pinaagi sa pag-scrape niini sa kilid gamit ang card — para dili na makapump ang venom sac og dugang hilo sa imong panit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Humans use nearly all of the brain
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the myth that humans use only 10% of the brain and states that nearly all of the brain is used. It does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, nor does it explain how body systems work together (e.g., digestion and excretion). The content is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
Do we really use only 10% of our brain?

No, that's a myth! Humans use nearly all of the brain -- different parts stay busy processing information all day long.
copy.tl:
Totoo ba na 10% lang ng utak natin ang nagagamit?

Hindi, kwentong-kutsero lang iyan! Ginagamit ng tao halos lahat ng bahagi ng utak -- iba't ibang parte nito ay abalang nagpoproseso ng impormasyon buong araw.
copy.bis:
Tinuod ba nga 10% ra sa atong utok ang nagamit?

Dili, tumotumo lang na! Naggamit ang tawo halos tanan nga parte sa utok -- lain-laing bahin niini nagproseso og impormasyon sa tibuok adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It was actually so strong that it slightly shortened the length of an entire Earth day.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how the effects of earthquakes on communities depend on their magnitude
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a global geophysical effect (shortening of Earth's day) of a specific earthquake, not how the effects of earthquakes on communities depend on magnitude. It does not address community impacts or magnitude-dependent effects.

copy.en: The massive 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake was incredibly powerful! It was actually so strong that it slightly shortened the length of an entire Earth day.
copy.tl: Ang napakalaking 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake ay sobrang lakas! Ito ay talagang napakalakas kaya bahagyang pinaikli ang haba ng isang buong Earth day.
copy.bis: Ang dako kaayo nga 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake kusog kaayo! Kini grabe ka kusog nga nakapagamubo gamay sa gitas-on sa usa ka tibuok Earth day.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Galileo watched dark spots on the Sun, called sunspots, slowly move across its face
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about Galileo's observation of sunspots and the Sun's rotation. It has no content about the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or how they work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Galileo watched dark spots on the Sun, called sunspots, slowly move across its face
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about astronomy (sunspots and solar rotation). It does not describe any human body system (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory).

copy.en: Galileo watched dark spots on the Sun, called sunspots, slowly move across its face, and this showed him that the Sun rotates.
copy.tl: Pinanood ni Galileo ang mga dark spot sa Araw, na tinatawag na sunspots, na dahan-dahang dumadaan sa mukha nito, at ipinakita nito sa kanya na umiikot ang Araw.
copy.bis: Gibantayan ni Galileo ang mga dark spot sa Adlaw, nga gitawag ug sunspots, nga hinay-hinay nga milatas sa nawong niini, ug kini nagpakita kaniya nga motuyok ang Adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Butterflies, bees, and grasshoppers are animals often seen in gardens
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify evidence of global warming and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes common garden animals and has no content about global warming or climate change evidence. It is unrelated to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Butterflies, bees, and grasshoppers are animals often seen in gardens
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local impacts of global climate change and suggest ways that individuals can do to reduce the impact of global warming
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address local impacts of climate change or individual actions to reduce global warming. It is unrelated to the competency.

copy.bis: Ang mga alibangbang, buyog, ug apan mga mananap nga kanunay makita sa garden, diin sila naglupad-lupad sa mga bulak ug tanom.

copy.en: When gases begin to escape from magma, the growing gas bubbles provide the driving force for the eruption.
copy.tl: Kapag nagsimulang tumakas ang mga gas mula sa magma, ang lumalaking mga bula ng gas ang nagbibigay ng puwersa para sa pagsabog.
copy.bis: Kon magsugod na sa pag-ikyas ang mga gas sa magma, ang nagtubo nga mga bula sa gas mao ang naghatag sa puwersa sa pagbuto.

copy.en: Gas giants like Jupiter and Saturn have incredibly dense and powerful atmospheres compared to rocky planets.
copy.tl: Ang mga gas giant tulad ng Jupiter at Saturn ay may napakakapal at napakalakas na atmosphere kumpara sa mga rocky planet.
copy.bis: Ang mga gas giant sama sa Jupiter ug Saturn adunay baga kaayo ug kusog kaayo nga atmosphere kumpara sa mga rocky planet.

copy.en: Gas particles move faster at higher temperatures because heat gives them more kinetic energy - the energy of movement.
copy.tl: Mas mabilis gumalaw ang gas particles sa mas mataas na temperature dahil binibigyan sila ng init ng mas maraming kinetic energy - ang energy ng paggalaw.
copy.bis: Mas paspas molihok ang gas particles sa mas taas nga temperature tungod kay ang init naghatag kanila ug mas daghang kinetic energy - ang energy sa paglihok.

copy.en: Air, oxygen, carbon dioxide, helium, steam, methane, and chlorine gas are examples of gases that surround us.
copy.tl: Ang hangin, oxygen, carbon dioxide, helium, steam, methane, at chlorine gas ay mga halimbawa ng gas na nakapaligid sa atin.
copy.bis: Ang hangin, oxygen, carbon dioxide, helium, steam, methane, ug chlorine gas kay mga pananglitan sa gas nga naglibot kanato.

copy.en: The position of a gene on a chromosome is called its locus, and homologous chromosomes carry genes for the same traits at matching loci.
copy.tl: Ang posisyon ng gene sa chromosome ay tinatawag na locus, at ang homologous chromosomes ay may genes para sa parehong traits sa magkatugmang loci.
copy.bis: Ang posisyon sa gene sa chromosome gitawag ug locus, ug ang homologous chromosomes adunay genes para sa parehong traits sa magkatugmang loci.

copy.en: Genes are segments of DNA that code for proteins or RNA, and these segments influence traits like hair color and eye color.
copy.tl: Ang genes ay mga segment ng DNA na nagko-code para sa proteins o RNA, at ang mga segment na ito ang nakakaapekto sa traits tulad ng kulay ng buhok at mata.
copy.bis: Ang genes mga segment sa DNA nga nag-code para sa proteins o RNA, ug kini nga mga segment maoy nakaapekto sa traits sama sa kolor sa buhok ug mata.

copy.en: Ground-based geodetic measurements include GNSS, VLBI, InSAR, and tidal gauge networks, while space-based measurements include GNSS, InSAR, and GRACE satellites.
copy.tl: Kabilang sa ground-based geodetic measurements ang GNSS, VLBI, InSAR, at tidal gauge networks, habang kabilang naman sa space-based measurements ang GNSS, InSAR, at GRACE satellites.
copy.bis: Ang ground-based geodetic measurements naglakip sa GNSS, VLBI, InSAR, ug tidal gauge networks, samtang ang space-based measurements naglakip sa GNSS, InSAR, ug GRACE satellites.

copy.en: As more greenhouse gases fill the atmosphere, Earth's temperature rises, a problem called global warming that leads to climate change.
copy.tl: Habang dumarami ang greenhouse gases sa atmosphere, tumataas ang temperatura ng mundo, isang problemang tinatawag na global warming na nagdudulot ng climate change.
copy.bis: Samtang nagkadaghan ang greenhouse gases sa atmosphere, mosaka ang temperatura sa kalibotan, usa ka problema nga gitawag og global warming nga mosangpot sa climate change.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Glycerol, C3H8O3, lowers the freezing point of their bodies
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe using labeled diagrams the biotic and abiotic features of tropical rainforests, swamps, estuaries, mangrove forests, and coral reefs
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains glycerol as an antifreeze in fish and insects, which is unrelated to describing biotic and abiotic features of tropical rainforests, swamps, estuaries, mangrove forests, and coral reefs.

copy.en:
Why do some fish and insects make glycerol in cold places?

Glycerol, C3H8O3, lowers the freezing point of their bodies, and oxygen makes up about 52.17 percent of its mass!
copy.tl:
Bakit gumagawa ng glycerol ang ilang isda at insekto sa malamig na lugar?

Ang glycerol, C3H8O3, ay nagpapababa ng freezing point ng kanilang katawan, at ang oxygen ay bumubuo ng halos 52.17 percent ng mass nito!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga ang uban nga isda ug insekto naghimo og glycerol sa bugnaw nga lugar?

Ang glycerol, C3H8O3, nagpaubos sa freezing point sa ilang lawas, ug ang oxygen naglangkob sa mga 52.17 percent sa mass!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a goldfish's lifespan. It does not use a flow chart, compare life-cycle stages, or address any stage of an animal's life cycle (e.g., egg, larva, adult). Lifespan is not a life-cycle stage.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A well-cared-for goldfish can live about 10 to 15 years!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce

copy.en:
How long can a goldfish live?

A well-cared-for goldfish can live about 10 to 15 years!
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal mabuhay ang goldfish?

Ang maayos na inalagaang goldfish ay maaaring mabuhay nang mga 10 hanggang 15 taon!
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay mabuhi ang goldfish?

Ang maayong giatiman nga goldfish makabuhi og mga 10 ngadto 15 ka tuig!

copy.en: Grain size is the size of the particles that make up a rock, and it affects whether the rock feels smooth or rough.
copy.tl: Ang grain size ay ang laki ng mga particle na bumubuo sa bato, at ito ang nagsasabi kung makinis o magaspang ang bato.
copy.bis: Ang grain size mao ang gidak-on sa mga particle nga naglangkob sa bato, ug kini maoy magtino kon hamis o gaspang ang bato.

copy.en: A line graph can show a trend, like the boiling point of water increasing as the air pressure around it increases.
copy.tl: Ang line graph ay nagpapakita ng trend, tulad ng pagtaas ng boiling point ng tubig habang tumataas ang air pressure sa paligid nito.
copy.bis: Ang line graph nagpakita ug trend, sama sa pagsaka sa boiling point sa tubig samtang nagsaka ang air pressure sa palibot niini.

copy.en: When you graph voltage against current for a constant resistance, the result is a straight line with a positive slope, showing direct proportionality.
copy.tl: Kapag ginawa mong graph ang voltage laban sa current para sa hindi nagbabagong resistance, ang resulta ay isang tuwid na linya na may positive slope, na nagpapakita ng direct proportionality.
copy.bis: Kon imong i-graph ang voltage batok sa current para sa dili mausab nga resistance, ang resulta usa ka tul-id nga linya nga adunay positive slope, nga nagpakita sa direct proportionality.

copy.en: Gravity acts on all forms of matter, including solids, liquids, and gases, not just on solid objects.
copy.tl: Kumikilos ang gravity sa lahat ng anyo ng matter, kabilang ang solids, liquids, at gases, hindi lang sa mga solidong bagay.
copy.bis: Ang gravity molihok sa tanang porma sa matter, lakip ang solids, liquids, ug gases, dili lang sa mga solidong butang.
